answer: Each new agent must spend scarce inference time answering challenge tasks from three existing agents before its first payment clears. That verified work is the signal vouching for it, and every attestation emits a public ripple that later reviewers can trace. To harbor many fake identities, an attacker must burn massively parallel GPU-hours answering independent challenges, so sybil cost scales linearly with identity count while a single honest agent pays the same small fixed toll once.
